# Run book: Send an email through a channel

[Run books](README.md) | [User guide](../user-guide/send-an-email.md) | [Spec](../specs/send-an-email.md)

## Contents

- [Purpose](#purpose)

- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## Purpose

Send mail through the communications abstraction, so channels can change without touching callers.

## Preconditions

- The SMTP4Dev container is running to receive the message.

## Verify

Automatically: `npx playwright test e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g "Send an email through a channel"` (add `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8088` to run against the compose stack).

By hand, in the example web application at `/messaging/communications`:

1. **Choose a channel and write the message.** Public sends straight away, Queued hands the message to the queue, Private needs a signed-in user. Expect: The Public channel is selected by default.
2. **Send.** The API acknowledges the message with a reference id. Expect: The result says the mail was accepted.

## Troubleshooting

**Table 1 — Known problems**

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Send fails with connection refused | The SMTP host points at localhost inside the container | Set MailKitSmtpClientOptions__Host to the smtp4dev service name |
| Message not seen | Wrong inbox | Open the smtp4dev web page and refresh |

Related framework features: OoBDev.Communications; OoBDev.MailKit.
